subject: BiotechX private deployment — connectivity & upgrade flow clarifications
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@biotechx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BiotechX private deployment — connectivity & upgrade flow clarifications

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the few clarifying questions we promised to follow up on so we can finalize the SOW and on-site readiness checklist.

Recap (from our side)
- You confirmed interest in a Private (air-gapped) deployment hosted in your facility (no outbound internet allowed).
- Target: 2 racks, each with 4x A100-class GPUs (customer-specified vendor).
- Priority items: offline upgrade process, hardware spares, KMS key handling, and maintenance windows.

Open questions / action items
1) Air-gap level: can you confirm whether a temporary jump host / maintenance laptop used during upgrades is acceptable when physically escorted (we discussed escorted removable media flow)?
2) Hardware vendor/model: please confirm exact SKU for the GPU servers (make/model/firmware baseline) so we can pre-validate driver/firmware compatibility.
3) Network topology: we need a redacted network diagram (DMZ, jump host VLANs, firewall rules) and the allowed egress/control-plane IP ranges if any (for out-of-band support).
4) Maintenance windows: you mentioned a monthly 03:00–05:00 local window for major ops — is that the only window or do you have an overnight weekend option for disruptive upgrades?
5) Spares & replacement: confirm whether you plan to keep hot spare GPUs/servers on-site or expect Redwood to ship spares under an RMA SLA.
6) KMS/HSM: confirm whether keys must remain on customer HSM or if we can use a customer-managed KMS bridge (we will not persist keys offsite).

Attached: redwood_private_requirements_checklist.pdf — this is our internal checklist; please fill in the shaded fields and return.

Next steps:
- If possible, send the redacted network diagram + facility rack/power spec (we need PDU and breaker per-rack details).
- We'll draft a minimal MOP (maintenance-of-procedure) for the offline upgrade path and share it with Vivek for any technical questions.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate schedules for a focused technical run-through next week once we have the diagram and SKUs.

—Michael

From: Ellen Shaw <ellen.shaw@biotechx.com>

Cc: BiotechX Ops <ops@biotechx.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BiotechX private deployment — connectivity & upgrade flow clarifications

Hi Michael — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers below and one follow-up question.

Responses:
- Air-gap policy: We are strict — no outbound traffic from production racks. Temporary jump host is acceptable for maintenance only if it is physically present in the room and supervised by our on-site engineer. No Wi‑Fi allowed.
- Hardware: Planned vendor is HPE ProLiant DL385 Gen11 (4x A100 equivalent per chassis). We will confirm exact SKUs/part numbers by EOD Friday.
- Network diagram: attaching the facility_rack_power and a redacted VLAN diagram; firewall rules will be emailed by our network team separately (expect that Monday).
- Maintenance windows: monthly 03:00–05:00 PT is the default. We can do a single weekend 02:00–06:00 maintenance if necessary for a disruptive upgrade, provided 14 days notice.
- Spares: we prefer to keep 1 hot-spare chassis on-site; we will also accept vendor RMAs for GPU replacements.
- KMS: keys must stay in our HSM. Any upgrade flow that requires image signing must accept our HSM-signed artifacts or support a handoff via an escorted USB key.

Follow-up question: you mentioned pre-staging an upgrade bundle — can you outline the offline upgrade MOP at a high level (steps / estimated downtime)? That will help our change board approve the work.

Attaching: facility_power_rack_spec.xlsx

Thanks,
Ellen

ellen.shaw@biotechx.com | +1 (617) 555-2020

Subject: Re: BiotechX private deployment — connectivity & upgrade flow clarifications

Hi Ellen — thanks for the quick answers and for the rack spec. I’m Monica from Solutions (looping Vivek for the technical detail). Below is a concise, high-level offline upgrade MOP we can use for your change board. I’ve noted where we’ll need signoff or customer action.

High-level offline upgrade MOP (summary)
1) Pre-validation (no downtime)
   - Redwood provides a signed upgrade bundle (image + drivers + model binaries).
   - Customer verifies signature via HSM or returns the bundle on a checksum-protected USB to Redwood for verification.
   - Test bundle on 1 staging node (can be a non-production chassis) to validate boot and driver handshake.
2) Maintenance window: bring production node(s) into maintenance one rack at a time.
   - Quiesce workloads and take a synced snapshot of models and config (we provide tooling).
   - Apply firmware and OS updates (estimated 30–45 min per host for driver/firmware updates; model cache warm-up additional 15–30 min).
   - Validate service health; run smoke prompts and perf tests from the staging node before returning to production.
3) Rollback plan
   - Retain pre-upgrade images locally; if rollback needed, reimage from local cartridge (USB) or local staging node.
   - Estimated rollback time: 45–60 min per host.
4) Post-upgrade validation and QA
   - 2 hours of automated acceptance tests + one manual test case run by your on-site engineer.

Notes / requirements from BiotechX
- On-site engineer required for removable-media flow; Redwood engineer can be present by video but will not handle physical keys.
- We recommend provisioning 1 temporary staging chassis (can be lower GPU count) to reduce risk.
- For HSM-signed bundle workflow, we will provide a short script to validate signatures against your HSM public keys.

Attachments and next docs
- I’ve attached a draft MOP (redwood-offline-upgrade-mop.docx) with more detail and a checklist for the change board.
- Vivek: can you review the estimated per-host timings and confirm we’re comfortable with the 30–45 min firmware window for the HPE chassis?

If this looks good, Michael will draft a short SOW + timeline and we’ll aim to present to your change board next Tuesday.

Thanks — Monica

Monica / Michael — this is very helpful and exactly what the board needs. A few quick confirmations:
- The removable-media + HSM signature approach is acceptable to our security team (I’ll circulate to them).
- We will provision a staging chassis (we’ll confirm chassis serial by Friday).
- We accept the 14-day notice for weekend maintenance windows — we’ll plan to approve a single weekend slot if needed.

Next actions:
1) Please send a one-page SOW draft (high level timeline + deliverables + acceptance criteria) — we’d like to review before the change board meeting.
2) Share an availability grid for the technical run-through next week (we prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT).
3) Provide a short note on warranty/impact to vendor warranty if Redwood performs image installation (we need this for procurement).

I’ll have our network team send the firewall rule set on Monday. Thanks — looking forward to the next call.

—Ellen
